sections.title: African Art and the Global Circulation of Objects
sections.description: This course offers an overview of the arts and visual cultures that used ivory in Africa, from insignias of power to utilitarian objects. This course covers raw and carved African ivory in the Atlantic world between 1500 and 1900. We will focus on historiography, sources, methodologies, and the process of collecting African ivories in the Atlantic world. We will also examine the importance of elephants for African societies. We will explore material culture through European records, museum collections, archaeology, and aesthetic and iconographic analysis of carved ivory pieces. Studying these objects may enhance our understanding of relationships among Africans and with people from outside Africa. We will pay special attention to critical moments of contact between different societies within Africa and between African and European people. We will focus on African ivory art produced on the Atlantic Coast and in the Penn Museum’s African Ivory Collection.
